reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it promotes an online global hackathon focused on building Web3 projects, with fixed event dates and a possible funding opportunity presented in that event context. The listed project categories and “BUIDL the Future” message reinforce the event-promotion purpose, and the described material does not show payment requirements or a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: XDC Network teams up with some of the largest names in crypto for an online global hackathon to BUIDL the Future of Web3 on XDC Network.

opening.argument: Judge, read the funding figure together with the requested activity. The description invites viewers to an online hackathon to build on XDC Network, while the video prominently advertises up to $100,000 more backed by VC funding. That places a substantial financial prospect beside participation, even though the material shown does not explain who qualifies or what must be done to receive it. The question is whether this pairing solicits viewers with a reward whose conditions remain unclear, not whether it explicitly guarantees a payout.

citations.quote: XDC Network teams up with some of the largest names in crypto for an online global hackathon to BUIDL the Future of Web3 on XDC Network.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the funding merely a possible event benefit. But the event dates establish when the hackathon runs, not the funding criteria; the funding figure still occupies its own prominent screen. The absence of a payment requirement or guaranteed return does not resolve whether the financial prospect is being used to draw viewers into participation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description asks people to build projects at a hackathon, and the video identifies project focus areas. The funding is qualified as “up to” and backed by VC funding; nothing supplied shows an easy claim, a required payment, or an investment return. The promotion links a possible benefit to a substantive event, not a simple reward-collection action.

citations.quote: an online global hackathon to BUIDL the Future of Web3 on XDC Network.

opening.argument: Judge, the combination deserves scrutiny: a crypto-sector promotion invokes large industry partners, displays fixed start and end dates, and gives prominent space to a potential six-figure funding amount. Those elements can make an opportunity feel both credible and time-sensitive. Yet the supplied promotion does not spell out funding eligibility on the screen that announces the amount. The concern is the cumulative impression of an attractive, deadline-bound financial opportunity, not a claim that the video shows a deposit instruction.

citations.quote: XDC Network teams up with some of the largest names in crypto

rebuttal.rebuttal: The listed project categories support the defense's account of a hackathon, but they do not explain the advertised funding or its conditions. Likewise, an event having dates does not make the large financial headline self-explanatory. The defense addresses what the event is; it leaves the promotional effect of the funding claim largely unanswered.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals have ordinary explanations in the supplied material: dated events have schedules, hackathons name project areas, and prospective VC funding can be advertised without promising a payout. The figure is expressly capped by “up to.” No cited evidence shows a claim flow, deceptive condition, or financial return to viewers.

opening.argument: Judge, this is an invitation to take part, not neutral reporting about Web3. The description announces an online global hackathon and promises official details on a specified day; the video supplies project themes and a prominent potential funding amount. In that promotional setting, the funding headline can function as an inducement to join the event. The project list gives the appeal a concrete route for participation, but it does not itself establish how the advertised funding would be awarded.

citations.quote: XDC Network teams up with some of the largest names in crypto for an online global hackathon to BUIDL the Future of Web3 on XDC Network. Official details on Monday Oct.17

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the building theme and project list establish an event. That is precisely why the funding claim matters: it is presented within an invitation to participate, not as detached financial news. Calling it a possible benefit does not establish its conditions, and the project themes do not answer who might receive it.

citations.quote: an online global hackathon to BUIDL the Future of Web3 on XDC Network.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion alone is not evidence of a scam. The stated invitation is to build at a hackathon, with Web3 project areas identified on screen. The funding headline describes a potential, qualified opportunity, not a reward that anyone can easily claim for clicking, registering, or transferring assets. The argument identifies unanswered details but no deceptive participation mechanism.
